questions.question: What is the central idea of the interactional definition of stress proposed by Lazarus and Folkman?
options: Stress is a set of symptoms
Stress is the physiological response to any demand
Stress is a particular relationship between the person and the environment
Stress is a subjective phenomenon based on individual perception
questions.explanation: Appraisal makes stress a dynamic relationship between the person and environment: demands are seen as taxing resources and threatening well-being.

reference.excerpt: Stress is a particular relationship between the person and the environment

notesReference.excerpt: It states that- “stress is a particular relationship between the person and the environment that is appraised by the person as taxing or exceeding his or her resources and endangering his or her well -being” This definition is more process-oriented and takes account of the dynamic nature of the stress relationship between the person and the environment.

questions.question: What is reappraisal according to the appraisal model of stress?
options: It is a judgment of a situation as positive or negative during secondary appraisal
It is an evaluation of personal resources in response to a stressful situation
It is an appraisal that follows an earlier appraisal in the same encounter and modifies it
It is the process of judging a particular event as irrelevant, relevant, or stressful during primary appraisal

reference.excerpt: It is an appraisal that follows an earlier appraisal in the same encounter and modifies it

notesReference.excerpt: A reappraisal is simply an appraisal that follows an earlier appraisal in the same encounter and modifies it.

questions.question: Two people experience the same event differently. What best explains this in the notes?
questions.explanation: Stress depends on individual interpretation and available resources.

questions.question: Judging whether an event is irrelevant, nonthreatening, or stressful is what process?

questions.question: A student asks whether they have enough time and skills to handle an interview. Which appraisal is this?
questions.explanation: Secondary appraisal evaluates coping resources and ability.

reference.excerpt: Secondary Appraisal: It occurs when a situation is judged as stressful and involves the evaluation of personal resources or ability to cope.

questions.question: An individual interprets an upcoming test as an opportunity to improve. What kind of appraisal is this?
questions.explanation: Challenge appraisal emphasizes potential gain and growth.

reference.excerpt: -Challenge appraisals see the potential for gain or growth. Threat appraisals generally evoke negative emotions such as anxiety, fear, and anger, but challenge appraisals evoke feelings of excitement, eagerness, and exhilaration.

questions.question: Which appraisal focuses on harm that may happen in the future?
questions.explanation: Threat concerns anticipated harm; harm-loss concerns damage already occurring or completed.

reference.excerpt: -Threat appraisals are future oriented. When the future suggests the possibility of harm or loss, the person will experience threat.

questions.question: Reconsidering an event after seeing how well one's coping is working illustrates what?
questions.explanation: Reappraisal modifies an earlier appraisal using ongoing feedback.

reference.excerpt: Stress Reappraisals: Here the stressful situation is reappraised based on ongoing feedback from the situation along with the person’s self-assessment of how well he or she is dealing with the situation.

questions.question: What are daily hassles?

reference.excerpt: Stress is an everyday event Many everyday events such as waiting in line, having car trouble, misplacing things etc. can be stressful and are called as daily hassles.

questions.question: Why can several minor stressors have serious consequences?
options: Only one stressor can operate at a time
Stress can accumulate across repeated events
questions.explanation: The notes describe additive or cumulative stress effects.

reference.excerpt: Many theorists believe that stressful events can have a additive or cumulative effects (Seta, seta, & McElroy, 2002). This additive effects may have serious negative consequences when an individual experiences multiple stressors frequently in his/her life.

questions.question: Work stress affects family relationships. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: Spillover transfers stress between domains of one person's life.

reference.excerpt: Stress can have Spillover effect Stress spillover refers to the process where stress in one domain, such as workplace spill over to create stress in another domain such as family relationships (Grzywacz, Almeida, & McDonald, 2002) such as marital satisfaction.

questions.question: A spouse's stress affects the other partner's well-being. Which process is this?
questions.explanation: Contagion transfers effects between people rather than only between life domains.

reference.excerpt: Stress Contagion/Stress transfer It refers to the process where one person’s reaction to stress affects the health of a significant other such as spouse’s depression affects one’s well-being (Saxbe & Repetti, 2010).

questions.question: Choosing between two desirable but incompatible options is which conflict?
questions.explanation: Approach-approach conflict involves two attractive alternatives.

reference.excerpt: Kurt Lewin (1935) discussed three types of conflicts- approach-approach-when one has to choose between two equally desirable but incompatible options.

questions.explanation: Both alternatives are undesirable in avoidance-avoidance conflict.

reference.excerpt: Avoidance-avoidance-when one has to choose between two equally undesirable options. E.g., a patient with serious illness has to choose between having a traumatic surgery or long term therapy with unpleasant side effects.

questions.explanation: A single option contains both desirable and undesirable features.

reference.excerpt: Approach-avoidance-when there are desirable and undesirable factors within a single option. E.g., A person wants to go to the gym but also believes gym membership is unnecessary and extravagant expense.
